title: Explainable SLA delta: proactive throttle + kernel hedge and telemetry enrichment
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Several high-volume customers reported a 20–45% increase in time-to-first-token (TTFT) for interactive chat workloads starting 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC. The regression is present across Hosted and Dedicated, with sporadic reports from Private (customer-managed clusters) where model variants and kernel builds differ. Immediate customer-facing symptoms: slow first byte, longer priming, and reduced tokens/sec for models in the 7B–70B family when request concurrency spikes.

Scope & observed behavior:
- Affected models: mix of Llama-derived 7B/13B quantized variants and a small number of 70B FP16 variants used by enterprise customers.
- Deployments impacted: primarily hosted clusters in us-west/eur-central, Dedicated pools with mixed GPU types, and isolated Private clusters where hybrid kernels were in use.
- Symptom window: regression onset correlated with a lightweight rollout of a kernel selection heuristic change (kernel-selector v2.9) deployed 2026-03-08 23:40 UTC.
- Telemetry: increased scheduler preemptions, longer kernel warmup time, and more KV cache misses for long-context priming sequences. Also saw a spike in RPC retry rate between router and worker (0.4% -> 2.7%).

Root-cause hypothesis: 
- Primary hypothesis: kernel-selector v2.9 introduced an aggressive 'stride-merging' heuristic that prefers a single larger kernel instance for throughput optimization. Under high fanout/heterogeneous model mixes this causes transient kernel preemption and cold-starts for certain kernels that don't match quantization profile, amplifying TTFT and reducing tokens/sec.
- Secondary hypothesis: scheduler's priority lane interactions plus the new kernel choice increase KV cache eviction frequency for long priming requests, increasing backend recomputation.

Immediate mitigations applied (observed positive effect):
1) Rolled back kernel-selector v2.9 to v2.8 on hosted and dedicated in us-west/eur-central (hot rollback): partial recovery in TTFT (~12–18% improvement within 12m after rollback).
2) Emergency per-model soft-throttle at the router (cap concurrency for affected models to 40%) to avoid warmup thrashing — reduced customer error surface while we stabilize.
3) Deployed a temporary KV prefetch pin for long-context priming sequences to avoid repeated misses (experimental flag).

Deliverables / Plan for hotfix + permanent fix:
- Short-term (next 72 hours):
  * Stabilize by fully rolling back kernel-selector v2.9 globally (Target: 2026-03-15 03:00 UTC) and lift soft-throttles after 6h of stable telemetry.
  * Ship a small scheduler patch to reduce preemption aggressiveness when kernel warmup rate is high (hotpatch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7642).
  * Add runbook steps and new dashboard panels that surface kernel warmup events, KV miss loops, and per-model warmup counters.
- Mid-term (1–2 sprints):
  * Rework kernel-selector to include per-model quantization compatibility scoring and fallback cost model; add a conservative sampling phase before globally enabling aggressive heuristics.
  * Improve KV cache admission temporality (give priming contexts sticky admission for 60s).
  * Expand unit and integration tests that simulate heterogenous fanout + mixed-quant kernels.
- Long-term:
  * Compile a 'kernel-compatibility matrix' by GPU type + quantization level to inform automatic kernel selection.

Telemetry & observability changes (required before rollback completion):
- Add a derived metric: kernel_warmup_rate_{model,region,variant} and an alert for >15% delta over baseline.
- Add a flamegraph hook and short-term trace sampling for requests that hit >1.5s priming time.
- Dashboard link for on-call: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ttft/ttft-rootcause-503999

Customer communication & bridge:
- Active bridge created with Support and Solutions: case RED-20260310-41 (customers: BrightLaw, FinSentry, RetailQ).
- Templates prepared: initial notification, mitigation updates, and postmortem summary.
- Commitment: performant baseline restored or a clear ETA for full remediation within 72 hours.

Safety & rollback plan:
- Rollback kernel-selector performed via config-layer (no code-level restart required) — immediate rollback is low-risk.
- Scheduler patch will be gated behind canary pools (10% traffic) with automated metrics gate checks.
- If regressions persist after rollback, escalate to full admission disable and route traffic to conservative model variants (quantized -> FP16) as fallback.

Acceptance criteria: 
- TTFT returns to within 5% of baseline for affected customers in each region for 6 continuous hours.
- No increase in 5xx error rate or user-visible token corruption.
- New telemetry panels show kernel_warmup_rate within expected ranges and KV eviction loops < 0.5% of priming requests.

Notes: This ticket captures both the customer escalation bridge and the actionable engineering plan to remediate, harden, and prevent recurrence. Follow-on tickets will split out the mid/long-term work (kernel-selector refactor, KV admission changes).
